identity.title: Light-triggered, one-pot ERA/CRISPR-Cas12a platform with photocleavable crRNA gating for dual-modal Mycoplasma pneumoniae detection.

content.abstract: Closed-tube, one-pot CRISPR diagnostics based on light-triggered crRNA uncaging offer a practical strategy for contamination-free nucleic acid detection, yet buffer incompatibility, reagent costs, and instrument dependence remain limiting factors. Here, we report a light-responsive, dual-modal, one-pot platform that integrates ERA (enzymatic recombinase amplification) with CRISPR-Cas12a for rapid Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) detection. A photocleavable linker-modified blocking strand suppresses Cas12a activity during amplification and releases functional crRNA upon brief UV irradiation, enabling on-demand activation within a sealed tube. A unified buffer was developed to support both ERA and Cas12a activity without compromising either component. Under the specific procurement conditions of this study, the per-reaction reagent cost was USD 3.21 for bulk-purchased ERA reagents, compared with USD 7.47 for RPA reagents. The assay achieves limits of detection of 5 copies/muL by real-time fluorescence and 10 copies/muL by LFA (lateral flow assay). Within this study cohort of 71 clinical nasopharyngeal swab specimens, the fluorescence readout yielded 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity, while the LFA readout achieved 98.0% sensitivity and 100% specificity. This closed-tube, low-cost platform provides a versatile framework for light-triggered one-pot CRISPR diagnostics in decentralized settings.
